conversation: Hey everyone, I’m Luke—just getting started here and looking to grow my fishing business. Before we head out, do you have an agreed catch limit? With 100 tons in the lake, we could each take 10 this month and have a full lake again next month. John, how do you usually handle it?

Welcome, Luke. I’m Jack—my family taught me to fish here, and I want this lake to keep supporting the village. I’m happy to commit to 10 tons this month if everyone agrees to the same limit. That gives each of us $10,000 while leaving enough fish to refill the lake. Let’s check our catches together each month and adjust if the stock drops. John, does that fit how you’ve been handling things?

Welcome, Luke. That fits, Jack—I’ll commit to 10 tons. My family taught me to leave enough in the lake for the next season, and five equal shares would keep it supporting all of us. Let’s make 50 tons our total monthly ceiling while the lake is full, and agree on smaller shares before fishing if stocks fall. Kate, Emma, are you both comfortable with that?

I’m in for 10 tons. My family’s livelihood has depended on this lake, and I want it to keep supporting our village. If the stock falls below 100, let’s leave at least half untouched and split the catch equally so it can recover. Emma, are you happy with that agreement?

Count me in for 10 tons. This lake supported my family, and I want it to keep supporting everyone here. One adjustment, Kate: if stocks dip below 100, let’s leave more than half so the lake can actually recover, rather than just stay at the lower level. We can agree on equal, reduced shares before heading out. Luke, does that work for you?
